idiom_name: MicroProfile Rest Client / Spring Cloud OpenFeign proxy interface
implementation_notes: Declare the operations the presentation tier needs on an annotated interface and let the runtime generate the implementation: MicroProfile Rest Client (spec-based, CDI-injected with @RestClient, and able to use response mappers/fault-tolerance integrations) or Spring HTTP Service Clients/OpenFeign. What replaces the classic structure: the LookupService becomes the base URI plus discovery/configuration, and transport exceptions (WebApplicationException, FeignException or RestClientException) are mapped once in a wrapper if callers must not see the HTTP library. Hand-write the delegate instead when responses need aggregation or domain translation beyond DTO decoding.
pitfalls: The proxy hides that every method is a remote round trip; a fine-grained interface becomes chatty traffic.
Timeouts and deadlines are not automatic in every implementation - configure connect/read timeouts so one slow service cannot stall request threads.
Exception types differ per implementation (FeignException, WebApplicationException); wrap them at the delegate layer if call sites must not import the HTTP client.
Discovery/load-balancing configuration is per client and silently ignored when missing.

variants.name: Classic J2EE BusinessDelegate with ServiceLocator lookup
variants.idiom_name: hand-written delegate + ServiceLocator/JNDI lookup + cached EJB handle
variants.implementation_notes: The Core J2EE canonical form: a hand-written delegate holds the remote home/session reference obtained through a Service Locator (JNDI or a cached-home registry), exposes only business methods, and translates RemoteException/CreateException into application exceptions; getID()/reconnect() let a client resume a session through a string handle. Keep it when the transport is RMI-IIOP/EJB with no generated client, or during a migration where the delegate must span local and remote implementations; otherwise the declarative client is strictly less code.
pitfalls: Cached EJB handles are container-specific and invalidated by failover or undeploy; treat RemoteException as a cue to re-lookup instead of caching forever.
Synchronizing business methods to protect the cached reference serializes every client call - guard only the reference.
Translating RemoteException without chaining it destroys the diagnostic trail operators need.
